name: Media flip-tile wall
doc: The picture on a wall of square tiles that turn over in 3D: every hit (onsets, at most one per `space` beats, louder = more tiles) flips a group of tiles (a scatter, a disc, a row, a column, a diagonal or a checker, rippling in) to show their part of the picture in another treatment (palette duotone, halftone dots, neon edges or a posterized mosaic), and flipping a tile again turns it back; on a wipe bar a sweep turns the whole wall to one treatment, and the next bar's sweep brings the picture back. At rest the tiles rock in a wave on each beat and the bass pumps and tilts them; a flipping tile lifts toward you and catches a palette light.

palette.doc: the treatments, the light on flipping tiles, the wall behind

gap.doc: space between tiles, share of a tile

flip.doc: seconds a tile takes to turn over

space.doc: beats between counted hits (onsets closer than this are one hit)

density.doc: how many tiles a hit turns

wipe.doc: bars on which a sweep turns the whole wall to one treatment (the next bar turns it back)

depth.doc: camera distance in tiles: lower = stronger perspective on a turning tile

wobble.doc: tiles at rest rock in a wave on every beat

glow.doc: palette light on a tile while it turns
